The wet weight of these neonates at parturition averages only about 0.0031 grams [Wwb = about 0.0031 grams], illustrating the minimal maternal investment per offspring that is characteristic of this highly fecund species. This small size at birth necessitates a period of rapid growth to reach critical developmental milestones, and the initial mortality rate among these tiny juveniles is often high due to predation and competition for food resources.

This relatively short developmental period allows for multiple generations within a single breeding season, contributing to the species’ ability to rapidly colonize new habitats.
